name: on-the-lesson

lesson.title: What a queue is
say: A queue holds work until a worker is free.
The sender never waits on the receiver.
explain: A burst piles up in the queue, not on the worker.

question: Why does a queue help with bursts?
good:
A queue **takes the burst**, so the worker never drowns.

Work waits in line until a worker is free, and the sender moves on at once. The lesson [What a queue is](lesson:l1) says it in its words.

name: another-lesson-covers-it
question: What is a cache?
good:
A **cache** keeps a copy close, so the next read is fast. It trades freshness for speed.

The pack covers it in [What a cache is](lesson:l2).
bad: A cache keeps a copy close. More in [Caching, the deep dive](lesson:l9).

name: beyond-the-pack
question: What year did a made-up standard body form?
good: I don't know. The lesson doesn't say, and I don't know of that body.
bad: A queue is a line of work that waits, and it helps because the work that comes in a rush can sit there while the worker takes one piece at a time, which means nothing is lost and nobody has to wait for the worker to be free before they send more, so the sender keeps going and the worker keeps a steady pace, and this is why queues are everywhere in systems that get bursts of work at odd hours.
